clue.text: Turn down drink at father's

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, and the 's carries over as an S
to sup is to drink, sip by sip

explanation.surface: Someone declines a drink offered at their dad's house.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse an offer or chance is to let it go by, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Location needs to be near a wide road

parts.note: a venue is a location for an event

explanation.surface: An event's site should be close to a broad street.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, often tree-lined.

clue.text: It provided food for energy after going without one valuable hotel provision

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
fed means provided food
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: going without means the after piece goes outside, around the one

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone's meal supplied the strength to carry on after a day's fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' looks like abstaining, but means placing outside; POST around I gives POSIT. 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels often provide a secure box for guests' valuables at reception.

clue.text: Does my pun revolve around Lewis Carroll, perhaps?

indicators.note: revolve around asks for the words to be spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A wordplay-loving writer asks whether his joke centres on the famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Dodgson; 'perhaps' shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll is the pen name of Charles Dodgson, an example of an assumed writing name.

clue.text: Why the play had to close — just one left on the Strand?

definitions.text: Why the play had to close — just one left on the Strand?

parts.words: Why the play had to close — just one left on the Strand?
parts.note: read as theatre: the play folded because its actors had departed; read again: a lone shipwreck survivor left on the beach, strand meaning shore

explanation.surface: A West End show folds, leaving one forlorn figure on London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street full of theatres, which makes the play reading plausible; strand also means a shore, where a shipwrecked sailor is marooned.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked person stranded alone on a shore fits the second reading of the whole clue.

clue.text: Rich incur debts on paper

parts.note: to cop is to receive or incur something, like a fine
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debt

explanation.surface: A wealthy person takes on written debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means abundant or plentiful, as rich can, in sense of a rich harvest.

clue.text: Tearaway sent at first to army base

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of sent

parts.note: a camp is a base for an army

explanation.surface: A young troublemaker is sent off to a military camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a milder kind of tearaway.

clue.text: Mentioned Scottish port in Skye Boat Song, perhaps

indicators.note: mentioned says we use how the port's name sounds when spoken

parts.note: Ayr is a port on Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: A Scottish harbour town gets a name-check in a famous folk song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song is a Scottish folk song about Bonnie Prince Charlie's escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or melody is called an air, and that song is one example.

clue.text: A page to write before Richard's dictated end of book?

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: dictated says the word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: Dick is a short form of Richard, so Dick's

explanation.surface: Someone writes a page before Richard dictates how the book ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick's, said aloud, gives DIX. The question mark flags the definition as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material placed at the back of a book.

clue.text: DIY shelf's hard to finish please take half back

indicators.note: to finish says the hard letter goes to the end of the shelf word

parts.note: the word shelf taken as written; the 's links it to what follows
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: back says those letters are read in reverse order
take half asks for the first half of the word please

explanation.surface: A do-it-yourself shelf proves difficult to complete, so someone pleads for it to be partly taken back.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the H of SHELF to its end gives SELFH; the first half of PLEASE, PLE, turned back by 'back' gives ELP.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY, do it yourself, is the spirit of doing things on one's own without outside help.

clue.text: Are bowled — run ahead — time's short!

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
up means ahead, as in being one up in a game
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator gasps as a batsman is out bowled and run out in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words bowled and run make the surface a match report; each just gives its scorebook letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt and short both describe a curt, brusque manner or a sudden ending.

clue.text: Put up money for entertaining key editor

parts.note: something entertaining is fun
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone bankrolls a party thrown for an important editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a project is to provide the cash or backing it needs.

clue.text: Friend's to turn informer on the other side

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague; the 's is a link meaning is
to sing is criminal slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A pal turns grass and goes over to the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO, from opposite number, is British informal for a mate or partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something puts one on the other side of a contest or argument.

clue.text: As writer he is performed, as speaker he is broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and reset

explanation.surface: A playwright's works are staged while his spoken words go out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As writer' and 'as speaker' make a neat balance; the second half is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is the playwright whose plays are performed everywhere.

clue.text: State expanded annually

parts.note: annually is p.a., per annum, and PA is also the postal abbreviation of a US state, here written out in full

explanation.surface: A nation grows a little more every year.
explanation.walkthrough: PA stands both for per annum, annually, and for a US state; expand the abbreviation into the state's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state with the abbreviation PA is named after William Penn.

clue.text: What might have you well oiled until bar and clubs turn out

definitions.text: What might have you well oiled

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned into a fresh shape

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Drinkers stay well oiled until pubs and clubs close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well oiled' suggests drunk; the definition means something that greases.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil or grease applied to machinery to reduce friction is a lubricant.

clue.text: European city hosts party in return — some Americans enjoy it

indicators.note: hosts says the city takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine

indicators.note: in return means the party word is turned around

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A Swiss city stages a party in exchange, and some American visitors love it.
explanation.walkthrough: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine; 'in return' turns the party abbreviation round before 'hosts' puts it inside. Baseball is the American national game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American national pastime, enjoyed by many US fans.

clue.text: Gory scene perhaps making a man be scared

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters that follow could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A grisly scene in a horror film frightens a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link; the fodder is all of 'a man be scared', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance of death is a medieval allegory of mortality, a scene of skeletons leading the living away.

clue.text: Mocking disorganised chaplaincy ——— helpers and priests initially made to leave

indicators.note: disorganised means put into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
made to leave means those letters are removed
initially takes the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A chaotic chaplaincy is ridiculed after its helpers and priests are forced out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, A and P from CHAPLAINCY to leave CLAINCY, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynical remark is sneering and distrustful, and so scornful or mocking.

clue.text: Drink about to come up in school

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down clue, come up means the word to is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Liquor is about to appear on the school premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' reads TO upwards in this down clue, giving OT; 'in' places the about-plus-reversal inside the school abbreviation. Scotch is Scottish whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland, a drink.

clue.text: Sit back on joining plane you'll get put off aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a kind of plane

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word sit in reverse

explanation.surface: Passengers are told to sit back once on the plane, or they will be put off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit back' looks like an instruction to relax in your seat, but 'back' turns the word round; 'joining' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw goods off a ship or aircraft to lighten it is to discard them overboard.

clue.text: See tons in public auction past the sell-by date

indicators.note: in places the tons letter inside the auction word

parts.note: a sale can be a public auction

explanation.surface: Weighty lots at an auction turn out to be out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is past its date is stale, no longer fresh.

clue.text: Performance after 6 is hit, in a big way

indicators.note: after places the performance piece behind the 6 piece

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a word for a rascal, and an imp is another such rascal
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A show that follows item six becomes a huge success.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to the solution of 6 down; a synonym of it, IMP, is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike with great force is to collide or make a powerful impact, a verb sense.

clue.text: Prohibit area importing a new fruit

indicators.note: importing means the first pair of pieces takes in the second, letting it inside

parts.note: to ban something is to prohibit it

explanation.surface: A region bans the import of an unfamiliar fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: A church makes one very good

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church produces someone excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert, someone outstandingly skilled at something.

clue.text: Spies are in outskirts of Taormina for the bread

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
in cricket, when you are in you are batting, so are in means bat

indicators.note: outskirts points to the outer letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: Secret agents lurk on the edge of a Sicilian resort while buying a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Taormina is a Sicilian resort, apt for an Italian loaf. 'are in' is the trap: it looks like a container, but it is a cricket phrase meaning bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat, open-textured Italian white bread.

clue.text: Plant being depressed by one passing perhaps?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling depressed
a passing bell is one tolled when someone dies

explanation.surface: A plant wilts sadly as someone walks past it.
explanation.walkthrough: A passing bell is tolled to announce a death; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a woodland flowering plant with blue bell-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Support article showing what babies do?

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece about supporting parents explains what infants get up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies grow their first set of milk teeth through the gums, a stage every infant goes through.
